segments.text: Outside the window, lightning flashes in a zigzag.
But air is actually a poor conductor of electricity.
Let's zoom into the tip of the bolt.
So lightning moves forward in short, choppy steps.
Each step bends toward wherever air conducts a little better.
Those weak spots in the air are scattered unevenly.
So each bent step links up into a zigzag path.
That's how the bolt outside got its jagged shape.
Lightning zigzags by bending toward whichever path conducts best.
